```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false
# Load packages
library(tidyverse)
library(brfssdata)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(broom)

# Read and recode BRFSS 2020 (same steps as the lecture)
brfss_lab <- read_brfss(
  2020,
  vars = c("_BMI5", "_AGE80", "_SEX", "_EDUCAG", "GENHLTH", "PHYSHLTH", "SLEPTIM1")
) |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  mutate(
    bmi       = bmi5 / 100,
    age       = age80,
    sex       = factor(ifelse(sex == 1, "Male", "Female")),
    education = factor(case_when(
      educag == 1 ~ "< High school",
      educag == 2 ~ "High school graduate",
      educag == 3 ~ "Some college",
      educag == 4 ~ "College graduate"
    ), levels = c("< High school", "High school graduate",
                  "Some college", "College graduate")),
    gen_health_num = ifelse(genhlth  %in% 1:5,  genhlth,  NA_real_),
    sleep_hrs      = ifelse(sleptim1 %in% 1:24, sleptim1, NA_real_),
    phys_days      = ifelse(physhlth %in% 0:30, physhlth, NA_real_)
  )

# Draw the same sample as the lecture, then keep the lab variables
set.seed(553)
brfss_lab <- brfss_lab |>
  select(bmi, age, sex, education, gen_health_num, sleep_hrs, phys_days) |>
  filter(bmi > 14.5, bmi < 60, age >= 18, age <= 80) |>
  drop_na() |>
  slice_sample(n = 3000) |>
  select(bmi, age, sex, phys_days, sleep_hrs)
```

```{r}

```

**Questions:**

a) Write the fitted regression equation in the form $\hat{Y} = b_0 + b_1 X$.

b) Interpret the **slope** ($b_1$) in context. What does it mean in plain English?

c) Is the intercept ($b_0$) interpretable in this context? Why or why not?

d) Is the association statistically significant at $\alpha = 0.05$? State the null hypothesis, test statistic, and p-value.


**Questions:**

a) Examine the **Residuals vs. Fitted** plot. Is there evidence of nonlinearity or heteroscedasticity? Describe what you see.

b) Examine the **Q-Q plot**. Are the residuals approximately normal? What do departures from normality in this context suggest about the distribution of `phys_days`?

c) Are there any influential observations (Cook's D > 4/n)? How many? What would you do about them?

d) Overall, do the LINE assumptions appear to be met? Which assumption(s) may be most problematic for this model, and why? *(Hint: think about the nature of the outcome variable.)*
